1. PURPOSE AND COMMERCIAL MODEL

ZeroOne agrees to provide the Client with access to its Point-of-Sale (“POS”) System under a Software-as-a-Service (“SaaS”) subscription arrangement.

The POS System may include sales processing, product management, inventory monitoring, reporting, cashier management, user administration, and other features expressly identified in the approved Feature Scope.

The System shall remain owned, hosted, administered, maintained, and managed by ZeroOne, except for any expressly agreed Client-managed components.

The subscription grants the Client a limited right to use the System for authorized business operations and does not constitute a sale or transfer of the software, source code, architecture, or other ZeroOne intellectual property.

2. SUBSCRIPTION PLAN AND FEATURE SCOPE

The Client's subscription shall cover only the features, modules, branches, terminals, users, integrations, and services expressly identified in the approved Feature Scope Checklist, Subscription Order Form, or other mutually accepted written documentation.

The approved Feature Scope shall form part of this Agreement.

Additional features, integrations, customizations, modules, or system modifications requested after approval of the Feature Scope shall be subject to ZeroOne's technical evaluation.

The Client acknowledges that the subscription does not entitle the Client to unlimited custom development, unrestricted system modifications, or unlimited integrations.

3. SUBSCRIPTION ACTIVATION AND GO-LIVE

The subscription shall commence upon the mutually confirmed Go-Live Date or another activation date expressly agreed in the Subscription Order Form.

“Go-Live” means the date the POS System is made available in the production environment for the Client's authorized operational use.

For multiple branches or phased implementation, the Parties shall document whether activation occurs separately for each branch or under a single subscription commencement date.

Continued use of the System shall be subject to an active subscription and compliance with this Agreement.

4. SUBSCRIPTION FEES AND PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS

All applicable subscription fees, setup or implementation charges, billing schedules, payment deadlines, minimum subscription commitments, and other financial terms shall be specified in a separate Subscription Order Form & Payment Agreement mutually accepted by the Parties.

The separate Subscription Order Form & Payment Agreement shall form an integral part of this Agreement and shall govern the Client's payment obligations.

Any changes to the agreed financial terms shall require written agreement between the Parties, except where adjustments are expressly permitted under the accepted Subscription Order Form & Payment Agreement.

4.1 SUBSCRIPTION ADJUSTMENTS DUE TO ADDITIONAL FEATURES AND INFRASTRUCTURE REQUIREMENTS

The Client acknowledges that the applicable subscription fee is based on the approved Feature Scope, system configuration, hosting resources, infrastructure capacity, and maintenance requirements at the time of subscription.

Should the Client request additional features, modules, integrations, users, branches, or other system enhancements that require increased server capacity, hosting resources, storage, processing power, bandwidth, technical support, or ongoing maintenance, ZeroOne reserves the right to propose an adjustment to the applicable subscription fee.

Any additional development, implementation, or integration charges shall be assessed separately from adjustments to the recurring subscription fee. Before implementing any change that results in additional charges, ZeroOne shall provide the Client with written notice of the proposed changes, including the revised scope of services, applicable fees, and effective date.

Any adjustment to the recurring subscription fee shall require the Client's written acceptance and shall be documented through an updated Subscription Order Form & Payment Agreement or other mutually approved written amendment.

If the Client does not accept the proposed adjustment, ZeroOne shall not be obligated to implement the requested additional features or infrastructure upgrades. The existing subscription shall continue under the previously agreed Feature Scope and commercial terms, subject to the existing Agreement and applicable law.

5. HOSTING AND SYSTEM ACCESS

Where the POS System is cloud-hosted, ZeroOne shall provide and manage standard hosting as included in the applicable subscription.

Hosting shall be subject to the agreed usage limits, infrastructure requirements, and applicable third-party service conditions.

The Client shall maintain suitable internet connectivity, compatible devices, and other operational requirements necessary to access and operate the System.

Offline operation, local data storage, and transaction synchronization shall be available only where expressly included in the approved Feature Scope.

ZeroOne shall not be responsible for interruptions caused by the Client's internet provider, incompatible hardware, electrical failures, or circumstances outside ZeroOne's reasonable control.

6. TECHNICAL SUPPORT

During an active subscription, ZeroOne shall provide qualifying technical support for the POS System and its approved functionality.

Technical Support may include:

• Troubleshooting system errors and unexpected behavior.

• Assistance with existing POS functionality.

• Investigation and correction of qualifying software bugs.

• Reasonable configuration assistance.

• Guidance on proper system operation.

• Corrective maintenance and applicable security updates.

Qualifying Technical Support shall not be subject to a fixed numerical limit unless otherwise stated in the Subscription Order Form.

Unlimited qualifying Technical Support does not constitute a guarantee of immediate resolution, continuous personnel availability, or round-the-clock assistance.

Support requests may be reasonably prioritized according to severity, technical complexity, operational impact, dependencies, and resource availability.

Technical Support does not automatically include new modules, major system redesign, custom development, new integrations, hardware repairs, extensive retraining, or on-site services.

7. MINOR ENHANCEMENTS

A Minor Enhancement means a small modification or refinement to existing POS functionality that remains within the approved Feature Scope and existing System architecture.

Examples may include minor interface adjustments, label changes, simple field modifications, small report adjustments, or basic validation improvements.

Qualifying Minor Enhancements may be included in the active subscription without additional development charges, subject to the applicable service package.

ZeroOne shall reasonably determine whether a requested modification qualifies as a Minor Enhancement based on its actual technical complexity, development effort, and effect on existing functionality.

Minor Enhancements do not include major reconstruction, substantial workflow modifications, new modules, complex integrations, or significant database restructuring.

Requests shall be scheduled according to reasonable development priorities and availability.

8. ADDITIONAL FEATURES AND CHANGE REQUESTS

Any feature, enhancement, integration, customization, or modification outside the approved Feature Scope may be treated as a separate Change Request.

Examples include:

• Additional POS modules or major features.

• Advanced inventory or accounting integrations.

• Additional reporting functionality requiring substantial development.

• New third-party payment integrations.

• Major changes to sales or inventory workflows.

• Substantial database or architecture modifications.

• Significant redevelopment or reconstruction.

• Custom integrations with external business systems.

ZeroOne shall evaluate the requested work and communicate the applicable scope, quotation, and estimated implementation schedule.

Separately chargeable work shall proceed only after Client approval.

A request shall not automatically become part of the agreed services merely because it was discussed, suggested, or demonstrated.

9. POS HARDWARE AND EQUIPMENT

Unless expressly included in the approved Subscription Order Form, the Client shall be responsible for acquiring, maintaining, and replacing hardware used with the POS System.

Hardware may include computers, tablets, barcode scanners, receipt printers, cash drawers, routers, and other peripherals.

The Client shall ensure that its devices meet the technical specifications communicated by ZeroOne.

ZeroOne shall not be responsible for hardware defects, physical damage, equipment incompatibility, or failures caused by third-party devices outside its supplied services.

Hardware installation, replacement, troubleshooting, and on-site assistance may be separately arranged.

Where ZeroOne supplies hardware, applicable warranty, ownership, replacement, and support conditions shall be documented separately.

10. THIRD-PARTY SERVICES AND INTEGRATIONS

Third-party services, APIs, payment gateways, licenses, communication services, and external integrations are not automatically included in the subscription unless expressly identified in writing.

Third-party services may include electronic payment platforms, SMS providers, accounting platforms, cloud services, and other external systems.

Their availability, pricing, limitations, and service conditions are determined by the respective providers.

ZeroOne shall not be responsible for service interruptions or changes caused by third-party providers beyond its reasonable control.

Any development work necessary to integrate or modify third-party services may require a separate approved scope.

11. SALES, INVENTORY, AND TRANSACTION RESPONSIBILITIES

The Client shall be responsible for the accuracy and completeness of information entered into the POS System.

This includes product descriptions, selling prices, inventory quantities, discounts, tax configurations, customer records, and other business information.

The Client shall also be responsible for supervising authorized employees and reviewing transactions, refunds, discounts, voids, and inventory adjustments.

ZeroOne shall not be responsible for financial discrepancies, inventory shortages, incorrect entries, unauthorized employee actions, or operational errors attributable to the Client or its authorized users.

Nothing in this section shall exclude ZeroOne's responsibility for losses directly caused by its own proven breach, negligence, or defective software, to the extent required by applicable law.

12. USER ACCOUNTS AND ACCESS CONTROL

The Client shall be responsible for managing authorized users and assigning appropriate access permissions.

The Client shall maintain the confidentiality of account credentials and promptly report suspected unauthorized access.

Administrative privileges shall be granted only to personnel authorized by the Client.

ZeroOne may provide access control and audit functionality as expressly included in the approved Feature Scope.

The Client shall be responsible for employee activities performed using legitimately assigned credentials, except where attributable to a security failure or other breach for which ZeroOne is legally responsible.

13. BIR REGISTRATION AND REGULATORY COMPLIANCE

The Client acknowledges that the POS System provided by ZeroOne is not currently registered or accredited with the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), where such registration or accreditation is required.

The POS System is intended for sales recording, inventory management, transaction monitoring, reporting, and other agreed business operations. It is not represented as a BIR-authorized invoicing system.

The Client shall be responsible for manually issuing the appropriate BIR-authorized invoices and other required tax documents to its customers, independently of the POS System.

The Client shall remain responsible for its business registration, tax compliance, statutory reporting, and other applicable regulatory obligations.

Should the Client wish to register the POS System with the BIR, ZeroOne may provide technical assistance, system documentation, and support in preparing the applicable registration requirements, subject to a separately agreed scope of services.

Any additional development, configuration, modification, or implementation necessary to meet BIR requirements may be subject to a separate quotation and prior Client approval.

ZeroOne does not guarantee BIR registration or approval, as such matters are subject to the requirements and decisions of the relevant government authorities.

Both Parties shall comply with their respective obligations under applicable Philippine laws and regulations.

14. DEMONSTRATION, ONBOARDING, AND TRAINING

Upon initial deployment, ZeroOne shall provide a complimentary system demonstration or onboarding session covering the primary approved POS functionality.

ZeroOne shall also provide a reasonable user guide or operating instructions for the agreed features.

Additional training, repeat onboarding, specialized instruction, and on-site sessions may be subject to separate arrangements.

15. SYSTEM MAINTENANCE AND AVAILABILITY

ZeroOne may perform maintenance, updates, security improvements, bug fixes, and infrastructure changes reasonably necessary to maintain the System.

Scheduled maintenance that may materially affect operations shall be communicated to the Client when reasonably practicable.

Unless a separate Service Level Agreement has been executed, no specific uptime percentage, guaranteed response time, or uninterrupted availability is promised.

ZeroOne shall use reasonable efforts to restore qualifying service interruptions within a commercially reasonable period.

16. OWNERSHIP AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

ZeroOne retains ownership of the POS System, source code, software architecture, frameworks, reusable components, templates, libraries, designs, improvements, and related intellectual property.

The Client receives a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to access and use the POS System during an active subscription.

Payment of setup, customization, subscription, integration, or development fees does not transfer ownership of the System or its source code.

Any transfer of intellectual property rights must be expressly agreed in a separate written agreement.

17. CLIENT DATA OWNERSHIP AND EXPORT

The Client retains ownership of its business records, sales transactions, inventory information, customer records, and other Client-provided data.

Upon termination or expiration of the subscription, the Client may request an export of available Client Data within thirty calendar days following the effective termination date.

ZeroOne shall provide available Client Data in a reasonable, commonly used electronic format supported by the System, subject to applicable law, security verification, and technical availability.

Custom data migration, restructuring, conversion, or transfer to another POS provider may require a separate agreement.

ZeroOne shall not be required to disclose proprietary source code or other protected intellectual property as part of the data export.

Data retention and deletion shall be performed in accordance with applicable Philippine laws, lawful retention obligations, and documented retention policies.

18. CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA PROTECTION

Each Party shall exercise reasonable care in protecting confidential business, technical, commercial, customer, and operational information received from the other Party.

Both Parties shall comply with applicable Philippine data protection laws, including the Data Privacy Act of 2012 and applicable implementing requirements.

The Parties shall establish appropriate safeguards for personal data and cooperate in addressing applicable security incidents and lawful data subject requests.

Where required, the Parties shall execute a separate Data Processing Agreement defining their respective data protection responsibilities.

19. CLIENT RESPONSIBILITIES

The Client agrees to:

• Provide accurate requirements and business information.

• Maintain compatible hardware and internet connectivity.

• Assign authorized system administrators and users.

• Properly train and supervise employees.

• Protect account credentials.

• Review and verify transaction and inventory records.

• Report system errors promptly.

• Cooperate with reasonable troubleshooting procedures.

• Comply with applicable business and regulatory requirements.

• Fulfill payment obligations under the separate commercial agreement.

Delays or interruptions caused by missing Client information, unavailable equipment, delayed approvals, or circumstances outside ZeroOne's reasonable control may affect implementation and service schedules.

20. NONPAYMENT AND SERVICE SUSPENSION

Subscription invoices and payment requests shall be issued in accordance with the accepted Subscription Order Form & Payment Agreement.

If an amount becomes overdue, ZeroOne may issue written payment reminders and provide a reasonable opportunity to settle the outstanding balance.

If the Client fails to remedy material nonpayment after reasonable written notice, ZeroOne may temporarily suspend access to the POS System, subject to applicable law.

Suspension shall not automatically terminate this Agreement or waive outstanding payment obligations.

Restoration of access may be subject to settlement of overdue amounts and completion of reasonable technical reactivation procedures.

21. SUBSCRIPTION TERM AND TERMINATION

The applicable subscription term and any minimum subscription commitment shall be stated in the separate Subscription Order Form & Payment Agreement.

Either Party may terminate the subscription in accordance with the agreed termination procedures and applicable Philippine law.

Where a minimum commitment applies, any early termination charges shall be governed exclusively by the accepted commercial agreement.

The Client may terminate for a material breach by ZeroOne that remains uncured after reasonable written notice and the applicable cure period.

ZeroOne may terminate for material breach by the Client, including material nonpayment, following appropriate written notice and an opportunity to remedy the breach where required.

Upon effective termination, the Client's right to use the POS System shall end, subject to agreed transition arrangements and the Client Data Export provisions.

Outstanding obligations properly incurred before termination shall remain payable.

22. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

Neither Party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, special, or consequential losses, including lost profits or business interruption, except to the extent such exclusion is prohibited by applicable law or otherwise expressly agreed in writing.

ZeroOne shall not be liable for losses attributable to Client-controlled hardware, internet connectivity, incorrect data entries, unauthorized employee actions, or third-party service failures, except to the extent caused by ZeroOne's own breach or legally attributable conduct.

Any agreed limitation on direct monetary liability shall be set out in a separately accepted commercial or service- level document.

Nothing in this Agreement shall exclude liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.

23. FORCE MAJEURE

Neither Party shall be responsible for delays or failure to perform obligations caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, widespread telecommunications outages, government restrictions, and other qualifying force majeure events.

The affected Party shall notify the other Party when reasonably practicable and take reasonable measures to minimize disruption.

Payment obligations already accrued shall remain subject to applicable law and the Parties' agreed commercial terms.

24. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the Republic of the Philippines.

The Parties shall first attempt to resolve disputes through good-faith discussion and written communication.

If no resolution is reached, either Party may pursue remedies available under applicable Philippine law before the appropriate court or tribunal.
